title: Global sections of the sheaf Hom complex identify ordinary cochains
statement: Let C be a site with topology J and R a sheaf of commutative rings. For arbitrary integer-indexed cochain complexes A,B of R-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], put H = Hom^bullet(A,B) [def-pur-hom-complex], using the internal Hom sheaves [def-pur-sheaf-hom], and let O be the rank-one free R-module sheaf. There exist additive equivalences e_n : Hom_R(O,H^n) ≃ Cochain^n(A,B) for every integer n, where Cochain^n consists of all families of module-sheaf maps A^p → B^(p+n). For i+1=j and every s : O → H^i, e_j(s followed by d_H) equals the usual external Hom differential δ(e_i(s)). No boundedness, acyclicity or injectivity is assumed.

source.place: Section 21.34 (Tag 0A8X), product construction and signed differential; global version Equation 21.34.0.2 (Tag 0A8Z). Read on https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A8X.

proof.text: Use SheafOfModules.unitHomEquiv and SheafOfModules.homObjSectionsEquiv to identify morphisms from the rank-one free module sheaf into homObj(M,N) with morphisms M → N. Their composite preserves addition and sends postcomposition with homObjMap(f,g) to precomposition by f and postcomposition by g; both assertions are definitional equalities in the existing constructions.

Obtain the actual Hom-complex product projections and differential formulas from homComplex_projections_exists. In degree n send s to the cochain with component e_{p,q}(s followed by π_{n,p,q}). Construct the inverse by the product-limit lift of the inverse component maps. The product projection identities and additive equivalence inverse identities prove both inverse laws. Additivity follows from add_comp and additivity of the factor equivalences.

Evaluate the differential on an arbitrary component p,q with p+j=q. Use the specified differential projection formula with q prime = p+i and p prime = p+1. Composition distributes over subtraction and integer-unit scaling; the factor equivalence preserves those operations and turns homObjMap into ordinary pre/postcomposition. Thus the component equals the postcomposition term minus i.negOnePow times the precomposition term. Mathlib δ_v uses j.negOnePow for the second term, and j=i+1 gives j.negOnePow=-i.negOnePow. Cochain extensionality proves equality.

lean.statement:
theorem homComplex_global_cochains
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max u v})
    (A B : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{max u v}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v} RingCat.{max u v})).obj R)) ℤ) :
    let R₀ := (sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v} RingCat.{max u v})).obj R
    let H := homComplex (R := R) A B
    ∃ e : ∀ n : ℤ, (SheafOfModules.unit R₀ ⟶ H.X n) ≃+
        CochainComplex.HomComplex.Cochain A B n,
      ∀ (i j : ℤ), i + 1 = j → ∀ s : SheafOfModules.unit R₀ ⟶ H.X i,
        e j (s ≫ H.d i j) = CochainComplex.HomComplex.δ i j (e i s)
